The '''Ōnakatomi clan''' (大中臣氏) was an ancient Japanese clan whose name derives from the use of "Ōnakatomi" as a surname. They were aristocrats and priests who oversaw [[Shinto]] rituals in the central government during ancient Japan.

== Overview ==
After {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|en|Fujiwara no Kamatari|qid=Q433995|lt=Fujiwara no Kamatari}} of the [[Nakatomi clan]] was granted the surname "Fujiwara," his son {{ill|Fujiwara no Fuhito|en|Fujiwara no Fuhito|qid=Q177517|lt=Fujiwara no Fuhito}} was still a child. Kamatari’s nephew [[Nakatomi no Omimaro]], who was also his {{ill|Son-in-law|en|Son-in-law|qid=Q3752578|lt=Son-in-law}}, temporarily succeeded as the head of the Fujiwara clan. Later, Emperor [[Monmu]] officially restored the Fujiwara surname solely to Kamatari's descendants, prompting Omimaro and others to revert to the Nakatomi surname. Despite this, Omimaro rose to the position of {{ill|Chūnagon|en|Chūnagon|qid=Q1185382|lt=Chūnagon}} (Middle Councilor). His son {{ill|Ōnakatomi no Kiyomaro|en|Ōnakatomi no Kiyomaro|qid=Q11431854|lt=Ōnakatomi no Kiyomaro}} gained prominence during the {{ill|Fujiwara no Nakamaro Rebellion|en|Fujiwara no Nakamaro Rebellion|qid=Q11623017|lt=Fujiwara no Nakamaro Rebellion}} in 764, supporting {{ill|Empress Kōken|en|Empress Kōken|qid=Q232955|lt=Empress Kōken}} (later Empress Shōtoku) and was rewarded with the surname "Ōnakatomi" in 769. Kiyomaro eventually rose to [[Senior Second Rank]] and [[:en:Udaijin|Udaijin]] (Right Minister).

During the {{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period}}, families within the Nakatomi clan were categorized into three houses known as the "Three Gates" ("Sanmon") as recorded in the "Nakatomi Genealogy."<ref>"Sanmon" refers to the three male descendants of [[Nakatomi no Katanoho]], [[Nakatomi no Mikeko]], and [[Nakatomi no Kokateko]].</ref> By the late 8th century, those in close relation to Kiyomaro adopted the name "Ōnakatomi."

The Ōnakatomi clan’s most influential branch, stemming from Kiyomaro, held hereditary positions as [[Department of Divinities|Jingi-haku]] (Head of Shinto Affairs) and [[:en:Saishu|Saishu]] (Chief Priest of the Ise Grand Shrine). Prominent figures include poets like {{ill|Ōnakatomi no Yoshinobu|en|Ōnakatomi no Yoshinobu|qid=Q1273650|lt=Ōnakatomi no Yoshinobu}} and [[Ōnakatomi no Suketomo]], as well as {{ill|Ise no Taifu|en|Ise no Taifu|qid=Q3072228|lt=Ise no Taifu}}, a renowned female poet.

By the late Heian period, the [[Shirakawa clan]] succeeded the Ōnakatomi as hereditary holders of the Jingi-haku office. The remaining members of the clan focused on regional shrine leadership and priesthood. The main lineage eventually became known as the [[Fujinami family]], a prominent court family in the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}.
